description: Mississippi State Board of Nursing (MSBN) transcript fraud detection rules

rules.description: Nursing program must be accredited by ACEN, CCNE, or NLNAC
rules.check: Verify the transcript or attached documentation references one of: ACEN, CCNE, NLNAC, or equivalent accrediting body. Absence of accreditation reference is a critical flag.

rules.description: Accrediting body name must be spelled correctly and in full
rules.check: Look for misspellings such as 'ACEAN', 'CCNEE', or abbreviated forms not matching official names.

rules.description: Graduation or degree conferral must be explicitly stated
rules.check: Transcript must contain a graduation date or degree conferred statement. A transcript without a conferred degree is incomplete for licensure purposes.

rules.description: Graduation date must be chronologically valid
rules.check: Graduation date must be after all listed coursework completion dates. Graduation occurring before the last semester's courses is a critical fraud indicator.

rules.description: Degree awarded must match nursing program (BSN, ADN, MSN, etc.)
rules.check: Verify degree type is a recognized nursing designation. Non-nursing degrees submitted as nursing transcripts must be flagged.

rules.description: Minimum nursing credit hours must be met
rules.check: ADN programs require minimum 60 credit hours. BSN programs require minimum 120 credit hours. Flag if total credits appear below program minimums.

rules.description: Clinical nursing courses must be present in curriculum
rules.check: Look for clinical practicum, clinical rotation, or nursing lab courses. A nursing degree without any clinical coursework is suspicious.

rules.description: Core nursing courses must be present (Fundamentals, Med-Surg, Pharmacology)
rules.check: Verify presence of foundational nursing courses: Nursing Fundamentals, Medical-Surgical Nursing, Pharmacology, Maternal/Child Health, Mental Health Nursing.

rules.description: Credit hours per course must be within normal range
rules.check: Individual courses should be 1–6 credit hours. Courses listed with 0, negative, or more than 8 credit hours are anomalous.

rules.description: Official institutional seal or stamp must be present
rules.check: Official transcripts must bear the institution's official seal, emblem, or registrar stamp. Absence of any official marking is a critical integrity flag.

rules.description: Registrar signature or certification statement must be present
rules.check: Look for a registrar's signature, official certification statement, or digital authentication mark. Unofficial transcripts lack these.

rules.description: Institution name must be consistent throughout the document
rules.check: The institution name in the header must match the institution name in the degree conferral section. Inconsistency suggests editing or tampering.

rules.description: Student name must be consistent throughout the document
rules.check: The applicant's name must appear consistently. Different name formats or spellings in different sections suggest the document may have been altered.

rules.description: Font and formatting must be consistent
rules.check: Look for inconsistent font sizes, styles, or spacing that could indicate text was inserted or modified. Highlighted, underlined, or bolded individual grades are suspicious.

rules.description: GPA must be mathematically consistent with listed grades
rules.check: If both individual grades and a cumulative GPA are listed, verify the GPA is plausible given the grade distribution. A 4.0 GPA with mostly C grades is fraudulent.

rules.description: Total credit hours must be consistent with course listing
rules.check: Sum the credit hours for all listed courses and verify they approximately match the total credits shown on the degree audit or transcript summary.

rules.description: GPA must be between 0.0 and 4.0 on standard scale
rules.check: Any GPA value above 4.0 on a standard scale, or negative GPA, is impossible and indicates document manipulation.

rules.description: Semester sequence must be chronologically logical
rules.check: Semesters must progress in order (Fall → Spring → Summer or sequential years). Out-of-order semesters (e.g., Fall 2024 appearing after Spring 2025) indicate tampering.

rules.description: Institution must be a real, verifiable educational institution
rules.check: The institution name should match a known accredited college or university. Fictional, misspelled, or unrecognizable institution names are fraud indicators.

rules.description: Course names must correspond to real academic disciplines
rules.check: Course titles should be recognizable academic subjects. Nonsensical, gibberish, or impossibly broad course names (e.g., 'Advanced Everything 101') are suspicious.

rules.description: Student ID format must be consistent
rules.check: If a student ID appears multiple times, the format and value must be identical each time. Inconsistency suggests the document was edited.

rules.description: Grade distribution must be statistically plausible
rules.check: An applicant with perfect grades (all A's) in every single course across 4 years warrants a note, though not a critical flag by itself.

rules.description: Transcript must be legible and complete
rules.check: Document should be clearly readable. Heavily pixelated, partially cut-off, or intentionally obscured sections of a transcript are formatting red flags.

rules.description: Page numbers or continuation markers should be present on multi-page transcripts
rules.check: If the transcript appears to be multiple pages, look for page numbers or continuation markers. Missing pages could hide failing grades or incomplete terms.
